The occupational-voice cohort records the edematous-polypoid form as only 8.5% of chronic laryngitis (catarrhal 46.7%, hyperplastic 23.2%); the edge records the polypoid-degeneration pathway, not a claim that chronic laryngitis usually produces structural lesions. governanceNotes: Authored conservatively at ASSOCIATION_ONLY strength: the lesion literature classifies Reinke's edema as a form of chronic laryngitis (a taxonomy-level overlap, not a progression claim), and the occupational cohort quantifies the edematous-polypoid form at 8.5%, but the shared-driver problem (smoking, reflux, voice overload cause both) means the inflammation-lesion distinction may be descriptive rather than causal.

Scope guard recorded: the catalog target spans nodules, polyps, cysts, AND paralysis; only the polypoid/edematous lesion spectrum is recorded here. Nodules and cysts are hyperfunctional-behavior lesions, and paralysis is unrelated to chronic laryngitis; no aggravation tier is drafted because hyperfunctional compensation for an inflamed larynx is itself a confounder rather than an established aggravation mechanism.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The benign vocal-fold-lesion review groups Reinke's edema as a form of chronic laryngitis within lesions of Reinke's space (nodules, polyps, cysts) and assumes a multifactorial genesis (Pickhard 2013); the occupational-voice cohort of 478 professional voice users found chronic laryngitis forms including catarrhal (46.7%), hyperplastic (23.2%), edematous-polypoid (8.5%), and atrophic (5.1%), with etiologic factors smoking, chronic tonsillitis, GERD, asthma, and diabetes (Stepanova 2019); the functional-dysphonia diagnostic-criteria series associated muscle tension dysphonia with vocal nodules, chronic laryngitis, or polypoidal degeneration, recording the hyperfunctional co-behavior confounder (Morrison 1986).
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level: the strongest source connection is taxonomic (Reinke's edema classified as a chronic-laryngitis form), the polypoid form is a minority of chronic laryngitis, shared etiologic drivers dominate, and the target identity includes lesion types and paralysis outside the recorded pathway, so no directional claim is made here.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A chronic-inflammation/Reinke's-space pathway is hypothesized: persistent laryngeal mucosal inflammation alters the Reinke's-space stroma, producing edema, fibrovascular change, and polypoid cord degeneration (polypoid corditis) that present as structural vocal-fold lesions; chronic cough and voice strain from the inflamed larynx add mechanical stress. The pathway is recognized in the lesion taxonomy, but smoking, reflux, and voice overload cause both conditions, so the relationship may be shared-driver rather than progression, and no directional claim is made here.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. The edematous-polypoid spectrum is recognized within chronic laryngitis, but individual determination requires laryngoscopic documentation of the specific lesion with chronology, exclusion of shared drivers as the primary cause, and review by a qualified medical professional.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Laryngoscopy/stroboscopy documentation of the specific lesion (polypoid corditis, polyp, nodule, or cyst) with chronology relative to the chronic-laryngitis diagnosis; smoking, reflux, and voice-use history quantified; exclusion of hyperfunctional behavior as the primary driver; explicit documentation that paralysis or other non-lesion components are not attributed to laryngitis; a medical professional's opinion connecting the documented findings in this individual case
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Smoking (the dominant shared driver of both chronic laryngitis and Reinke's edema)
Laryngopharyngeal reflux as an independent lesion cause
Vocal hyperfunction/abuse as the primary nodule-and-polyp driver
Occupational irritant exposure (fumes, dust, dry air)

suggestions.rationale: Authored conservatively at association-only strength: the taxonomy records Reinke's edema as a chronic-laryngitis form and the occupational cohort quantifies its rarity, but shared drivers defeat progression claims; the edge records the polypoid-degeneration pathway only, excluding the target's nodule/cyst hyperfunctional and paralysis components.
